levels.descriptor: Describes a club's playing style in a few words, for example how it presses and builds up.
Breaks a playing style into principles for each phase of play and spots them in a match.
Writes a club playing-style document that coaches, analysts and recruiters can apply.
Sets one playing style from academy to first team and checks that every department follows it.
Names the phase of play and each team's basic shape while watching a match.
Tracks off-ball players and explains why space opens or closes in a passage of play.
Explains in real time why one team is on top and what is causing it.
Teaches others what to watch for and checks their match reading against the footage.
Explains what a game plan is and which parts it covers: shape, pressing, build-up and set pieces.
Builds a simple plan for one opponent from a given opposition report.
Builds a full match plan against an opponent and turns it into a training week.
Owns the game plan for every match and adapts the method to the squad and the opponent.
Recognises when a match changes, for example after a goal, a red card or an opponent's switch of shape.
Suggests a substitution or a shape change and states the reason for it.
Makes in-game changes from live information and explains the effect afterwards.
Leads matchday decisions with the staff and sets how live input reaches the bench.
Names the main set-piece types and the roles players take in them.
Reads an opponent's set-piece routine from footage and points out its weak spot.
Designs attacking and defensive set-piece routines and coaches them in a session.
Runs the club's set-piece programme and agrees its training time with the head coach.
Lists what goes into picking a team: form, fitness, the opponent and the game plan.
Proposes a starting eleven with a reason for each choice.
Picks the team using medical, analysis and coaching input and explains each choice to the staff.
Owns selection and sets how fitness and medical advice feed into it.
Describes the parts of a training session and what each part is for.
Plans one session that trains one game-plan principle.
Plans and runs the week's sessions, adjusting them to match load and the opponent.
Leads the coaching staff's day-to-day training and checks the quality of their sessions.
Explains what an individual development plan holds: goals, clips and a review date.
Writes a development plan for one player from given analysis and coach notes.
Writes and reviews development plans for a group and links each goal to training and footage.
Sets the development-plan method for a squad or an academy and coaches staff in using it.
Describes how a season splits into pre-season, in-season blocks and congested periods.
Builds a block plan for a few weeks that balances matches, training and recovery.
Plans the whole season with the performance staff and adjusts it to the fixture list.
Owns the seasonal plan and aligns the coaching, performance and medical staff behind it.
Explains what an opposition report covers: shape, key players, strengths and weaknesses.
Builds a short opposition report from footage and data, with clips.
Produces the full opposition pack for each match and presents it to the coaches.
Leads the opposition-analysis process and sets the format and quality bar for the department.
Explains how analysts feed live information to the bench during a match.
Codes key moments live and flags them to a lead analyst.
Gives the coaches clear live and half-time input that they can act on.
Designs the live-analysis workflow and trains analysts to deliver it.
Explains what a post-match review checks against the game plan.
Builds a post-match clip set on agreed themes.
Delivers the post-match review of team and individual performance against the playing style.
Owns the review cycle and turns its findings into actions for coaching and recruitment.
Names the tools analysts use to code and clip video, such as Sportscode.
Codes a match with a given code window and exports clips.
Builds code windows from the game model and manages match and training footage.
Chooses the department's video tools and trains staff to use them.
Explains why a club follows its loaned players and what it watches for.
Logs a loanee's minutes, matches and footage over a few weeks.
Reviews each loanee's matches and footage and reports progress to the club.
Runs the monitoring programme for all loanees and sets the reporting standard.
Explains what a football model is for, for example estimating chance quality.
Fits and checks a simple model on event data with guidance.
Builds and tests models on event and tracking data that answer a club question.
Leads the club's modelling work and decides which approach fits each question.
Explains the difference between a model in a notebook and one that staff use every week.
Packages a model so that it runs on new data with given tooling.
Deploys a model, monitors its accuracy and fixes it when the data changes.
Decides which models reach production and sets how their accuracy is judged.
Explains why a model output is an estimate, not a fact.
Adds intervals or ranges to a model output with guidance.
Reports every model result with its uncertainty and explains it to non-specialists.
Sets how the department states uncertainty and coaches staff to communicate it.
Explains how match data moves from a provider into club tools.
Runs and repairs an existing data pipeline with a guide.
Builds pipelines and a warehouse that load event and tracking data reliably.
Owns the club data platform, its design and its quality standards.
Explains what tracking data records and how it differs from event data.
Loads a tracking sample and plots player positions for one moment.
Processes full-match tracking data at scale and joins it to events.
Sets the club's methods for storing and using tracking data.
Reads a football dashboard and explains what each chart shows.
Builds a simple dashboard from a prepared table.
Builds dashboards and self-service tools that staff use without help.
Designs the club's self-service platform and its standards for clear charts.
Reads a short Python or SQL script and says what it does.
Writes Python or SQL to filter and aggregate match data.
Writes tested, reusable Python and SQL code for analysis and pipelines.
Reviews others' code and sets the team's coding standards.
Explains how clubs find players: scouting, data and networks.
Watches a player and lists strengths and weaknesses against a role profile.
Identifies players who fit the role, the style and the budget, and builds a shortlist.
Has a record of identifying talent and sets how the club searches for players.
Explains what a scouting report holds and who reads it.
Writes a scouting report from live or video viewing in a given template.
Writes recommendations backed by data, reports and footage that coaches trust.
Sets the report template and grading scale and checks scouts' reports.
Explains how data can narrow a long list of players.
Filters and ranks players on given metrics for a role.
Builds a model that ranks targets for a role and presents the shortlist.
Decides how data and scouting combine in the club's recruitment process.
Reads a squad list by position, age and contract end date.
Maps the squad's gaps for the next season.
Builds a multi-year squad plan with succession for every position.
Owns squad renewal and aligns recruitment, academy and the head coach with the plan.
Explains how a scouting network is organised by region and level.
Assigns matches to scouts and tracks their coverage.
Runs a scouting network and moves its coverage to where the club needs players.
Builds the scouting, analytics and video structure that recruitment depends on.
Explains why character and style fit matter in a signing.
Gathers background information on a target from given contacts.
Assesses a target's character and style fit and records the evidence.
Sets how the club judges character and fit and makes it part of every recommendation.
Explains the parties in a transfer: clubs, player, agent.
Prepares a negotiation brief with fee and wage limits.
Negotiates transfers, loans or contracts inside agreed limits.
Leads the club's major negotiations and coaches staff in negotiating.
Names the parts of a player contract: length, wage, bonuses and clauses.
Compares two contract offers and their cost over time.
Designs contract structures that fit the squad plan and the budget.
Sets the club's contract policy and approves the structures used.
Explains why clubs loan players out and what a good host club offers.
Compares host clubs for a player on minutes, level and coaching.
Vets host clubs and places players on loans that fit their development.
Leads the club's loan strategy, placements and loan contracts.
Explains the roles of agents and other clubs in the transfer market.
Keeps a contact log of agents and clubs and their players.
Maintains working relationships with agents and clubs that open deals.
Builds the club's network of agents, clubs and loan partners.
Reads a club budget and names its main income and cost lines.
Builds a department budget and tracks spending against it.
Builds the club budget across football and business departments.
Owns the club's finances and decides budget priorities with the owners.
Names a club's revenue streams: broadcasting, commercial, matchday and player trading.
Analyses one revenue stream and suggests a way to grow it.
Plans commercial growth across sponsorship, brand and matchday.
Leads the club's commercial strategy and balances it with sporting ambition.
Explains what a club's sporting strategy covers: style, squad, academy and staff.
Writes how one department supports the sporting strategy.
Writes a multi-year sporting strategy and links it to recruitment and the academy.
Sets the club's sporting strategy and keeps it stable through changes of coach.
Explains how clubs hire coaches and specialist staff.
Writes a role profile and interview questions for one post.
Runs a hiring process and recommends a candidate with evidence.
Appoints the head coach and senior staff and plans their succession.
Explains what a department head does: people, process and standards.
Leads a small team on a defined task.
Manages a department's people and processes to a set standard.
Builds and leads a department and develops its staff into leaders.
Draws a club's football structure and its reporting lines.
Compares two club structures and their trade-offs.
Designs a department structure with clear roles and decision rights.
Sets the club structure and who owns each decision across football and business.
Describes what a high-performance environment looks like day to day.
Spots behaviours in a squad or staff that help or hurt performance.
Builds team routines and standards that keep performance high.
Sets and protects the club's performance culture across staff and players.
Explains who the stakeholders are: coaches, directors, owners.
Presents one finding with a clear message and a chart.
Presents analysis or recommendations quickly and clearly to mixed audiences.
Coaches staff in presenting and sets how insight reaches decision makers.
Explains why coaches and specialists often talk past each other.
Rewrites a specialist finding in coaching language.
Turns specialist work into actions that the head coach accepts.
Acts as the link between the head coach and all specialist departments.
Explains how owners, the board and the chief executive govern a club.
Prepares a short board update on one football topic.
Presents football plans to the board and wins support for them.
Represents football at board level and keeps owner support through difficult periods.
Explains how a coaching message reaches players: meetings, clips and one-to-ones.
Delivers one clear message to a player with a clip.
Delivers the coaching message to the squad on training days and matchdays.
Sets how the staff talk to players and filters issues before they reach the manager.

title: Injury prevention and return to play

levels.descriptor: Explains the main injury risks in football and why availability matters.
Reads an injury report and a return-to-play plan.
Plans prevention and return-to-play steps with the medical staff.
Owns injury prevention and return-to-play decisions for the squad.
Explains what training and match load mean.
Reads load data and spots players at risk.
Adjusts training load across the week from load data.
Sets the club's load-management policy and its link to selection.
Names the performance disciplines: sports science, medicine, conditioning, nutrition and analytics.
Explains what each performance discipline measures and why.
Works with each discipline's lead and uses their evidence in decisions.
Leads the performance disciplines as one department focused on availability.
Explains which governing-body rules apply to the club's area of work.
Checks one process against the governing-body rules.
Runs a programme that meets governing-body rules and audits.
Owns compliance for a programme and sets the controls that keep it.
Explains welfare and safeguarding duties towards players, especially young players.
Follows the club's welfare and safeguarding procedures.
Supports players' welfare on and off the pitch and records concerns.
Owns welfare and safeguarding standards for a programme.
Explains the pathway from academy to first team.
Maps one player's next steps on the pathway.
Plans pathways for a group of players with coaches and recruitment.
Owns the club's pathway and aligns academy and first team in one style.
Explains what an academy runs: coaching, education, logistics and recruitment.
Organises one part of an academy programme.
Manages an academy programme's staff, logistics and education.
Runs a sustainable academy focused on developing young talent.
